span: If you're unsure, it's completely reasonable to email them or ask after class: "I wanted to make sure I understood your comment—could you say more about what worked or didn't work with my approach?"
In corporate speak, **“let’s circle back on that” literally means “we will return to this topic later.”**
Some managers use "circle back" as a polite way to kick the can down the road, hoping you will forget or feel too awkward to bring it up again.
It means **the conversation has been paused, not ended.**
A good next step would be to follow up professionally after a few days, for example:
Want me to draft a short self-reported sick note or an email to your manager/HR explaining the Tuesday absence?
If you want, I can help you stress-test your system with questions about expectancy, drawdown, position sizing, and risk of ruin.
Let me know if you have any specific feedback or if you'd like me to suggest further changes!
Want help with any of these?
I'm glad to help you draft that in your own words.
let me know the tone you're going for
Want me to go deeper on any part — like quantitative easing, how markets react to Fed announcements, or historical examples (e.g., 2008 or 2022-2023 rate hikes)?
